영국 지도자들은 슈퍼마켓에 플라스틱 없는 구역을 두라고 촉구하고 있다.
→ Leaders are calling for supermarkets to have plastic-free areas.

노르웨이는 플라스틱 병의 97%를 재활용한다.
→ Norway recycle 97 percent of its plastic bottles.
questions.explanation: 주어 Norway는 3인칭 단수이므로 recycles로 써야 한다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 두 문장의 의미가 같도록 바꾼 것이 **잘못된** 것은?
choices:
It took about 80 years to build the pyramids.
→ Building the pyramids took about 80 years.

People use a trillion plastic bags every year.
→ A trillion plastic bags are used every year.

Most of this plastic will never biodegrade.
→ Most of this plastic will biodegrade soon.

Seattle became the first major U.S. city to ban plastic straws.
→ Seattle banned plastic straws before any other major U.S. city.

The workers usually had enough food.
→ The workers usually did not go hungry.
questions.explanation: never biodegrade(절대 생분해되지 않는다)와 will biodegrade soon(곧 생분해될 것이다)은 뜻이 반대이다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 **않는** 것은?
choices: 오늘날 약 83억 개의 플라스틱 빨대가 세계의 해변을 오염시키고 있다.
시애틀은 2018년에 플라스틱 빨대를 금지한 미국 최초의 주요 도시였다.
번다눈과 샌프란시스코는 생수를 완전히 또는 부분적으로 금지했다.
영국 지도자들은 플라스틱 테이크아웃 용기에 세금을 매기기를 원한다.
노르웨이 슈퍼마켓의 기계는 병 하나당 최대 2.5달러를 돌려준다.
questions.explanation: 환불금은 병당 최대 2.5크로네(32센트)이다. 2.5달러가 아니다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: What does the underlined <u>its example</u> refer to?
questions.explanation: 바로 앞 문장에서 시애틀이 플라스틱 빨대를 금지했다고 했으므로 its example은 시애틀의 빨대 금지를 가리킨다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Real Lives of the Pyramid Builders
The Tallest Buildings in the World
questions.explanation: 피라미드를 지은 사람이 누구였는지와 그들의 고된 삶, 음식·의료, 자부심을 다루므로 ③이 알맞다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: The builders' cemetery was found far away from the pyramids.
Only male skeletons were found in the cemetery.
Female workers generally lived longer than male workers.
The workers wrote *Friends of Khufu* because the king ordered them to.
The workers' bones show signs of arthritis.
questions.explanation: the bones show signs of arthritis. ①바로 가까이(Close by) ②여성 유골도 많이 발견 ③남성 40~45세, 여성 30~35세 ④국가적 프로젝트의 참여자라는 자부심 때문.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 (A) <u>tougher</u>와 의미가 가장 비슷한 것은?
questions.explanation: tough는 '힘든, 고된'이므로 tougher는 harder(더 힘든)와 가장 가깝다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: Which of the following best fits in (B)?
questions.explanation: 앞에는 힘든 삶(관절염·짧은 수명), 뒤에는 충분한 음식과 의료 혜택이라는 좋은 점이 나오므로 역접 However가 알맞다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 〈보기〉의 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

> Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm were two young men from Germany who loved reading stories. ( ⓐ ) As university students, they became interested in folktales—traditional stories or legends that people told again and again, often for generations. ( ⓑ ) The brothers began to collect folktales from storytellers all over Germany. ( ⓒ ) Between 1812 and 1814, the brothers published two books in German. ( ⓓ ) These included stories like "Cinderella," "Snow White," and "Little Red Riding Hood." ( ⓔ ) The collections became known in English as *Grimms' Fairy Tales*.

〈보기〉
> Many were similar to stories told in France, Italy, Japan, and other countries.
questions.explanation: 〈보기〉의 Many는 바로 앞에서 형제가 수집한 folktales를 가리키므로 ⓒ에 들어가야 한다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: According to the passage, which is **NOT** something the girl did in her brothers' home?
choices: She opened the door with her finger.
She cooked a meal for her brothers.
She drank a little from each cup.
She ate a little from each plate.
questions.explanation: 소녀가 오빠들을 위해 음식을 만들었다는 내용은 없다. ①~④는 본문에 나온다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A)수년 동안 멈추지 않고 찾았으므로 determined (B)부모님 반지를 '실수로' 떨어뜨림 accidentally (C)까마귀가 반지를 곧바로 '알아보았다' recognized.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 **다른** 것은?
questions.explanation: (a)(b)(c)(e)는 모두 소녀(여동생), (d) them은 식탁 위의 일곱 접시와 일곱 컵을 가리킨다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음은 윗글을 한 문장으로 요약한 것이다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

> Researchers have found new ways to (A)________ the soldiers' colors, and their next goal is to (B)________ the colors to the army again.
questions.explanation: 특수 액체로 색을 보존(preserve)하고, 다음 과제는 색을 다시 입히는(apply) 방법을 찾는 것이다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글을 읽고 답할 수 **없는** 질문은?
choices: 최근 발견된 구역에는 병사가 몇 구 이상 있었는가?
Rong Bo는 박물관에서 어떤 일을 하는가?
특수 액체는 어느 나라 연구진이 개발했는가?
액체를 뿌린 뒤 유물을 무엇으로 덮는가?
questions.explanation: 액체의 재료는 나오지 않는다. ①100구 이상 ③중국·독일 ④플라스틱 ②수석 화학자(고고학자).

groups.title: [15~16] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
groups.context:
> Once upon a time, there lived a man and a woman who had seven sons. The couple wanted a daughter, and, eventually, they had a girl who they loved very much. One day, the father needed water for the child, so he sent the seven brothers to a well in the forest to get it. Once there, though, the boys began to fight, and the water jug fell into the well. The boys did not know what to do. They were afraid to go home.
>
> Hours passed. "Where are those boys?" shouted the angry father. "They are probably playing a game and forgot about the water. I wish they were all turned into ravens!" When he looked up, he saw seven black birds flying away.
>
> ⋯
>
> Eventually, the ravens returned for their meal. The girl hid behind a door and watched. When the seventh raven drank from his cup, something hit his mouth. The raven recognized it immediately—it was his parents' ring. "I wish our sister were here," he said, "and then we could be free." Their sister quickly ran to them, and suddenly the ravens were human again. The brothers kissed their sister, and they all went home together happily.

groups.title: [17~20] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
groups.context:
> The first emperor of China, Qin Shihuang, is remembered for the many things he did during his rule. The emperor ordered the construction of a huge army of life-sized terracotta soldiers. These, he hoped, would protect his tomb after his death.
>
> Today, the soldiers in Xi'an's terracotta museum are light brown, but they weren't always this color. They began as an army of red, blue, yellow, green, white, and purple. Sadly, most of the colors did not (B)________ to the present day. Before their discovery, the clay soldiers were protected by being underground. When they were unearthed, however, the air caused the coating under the paint to fall off.
>
> New techniques are now starting to (A) <u>reveal</u> the army's true colors. Chinese and German researchers have developed a special liquid to help preserve the soldiers' colors. After they find a soldier or other artifact, archeologists spray it with the liquid. They then cover it in plastic.
>
> Archeologists are also finding colors in the dirt around Xi'an's terracotta warriors. It's important not to disturb the dirt, so the colors won't be lost. The next challenge, says Rong Bo, is to find a way to apply the colors to the army again. Once that happens, artists can bring Emperor Qin's army back to life in full color.

groups.title: [22~24] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
groups.context:
> The world has a plastic problem—and it is increasing. Scientists are working to find a long-term solution by making plastic more biodegradable. But in the meantime, here are five things you can do to (A)________ plastic waste now.
>
> Quit using plastic bags. Instead, take your own (B)________ shopping bag to the store. People use a trillion plastic bags worldwide every year. Roughly 10 percent are used in the United States alone. That's almost one bag per American per day. In contrast, the average Dane uses four single-use bags per year. In 1993, Denmark was the first country to place a tax on plastic bags.
>
> ⋯
>
> Recycle. We can't recycle all plastic items, but it is possible to recycle most bottles and milk or juice cartons. Today, Norway recycles 97 percent of its plastic bottles. How? Machines at most supermarkets take the bottles and give a (C)________ of up to 2.5 kroner (32 cents) per bottle.

groups.title: [25~26] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
groups.context:
**(A)**
> Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm were two young men from Germany who loved reading stories. As university students, they became interested in folktales—traditional stories or legends that people told again and again, often for generations. The brothers began to collect folktales from storytellers all over Germany. Many were similar to stories told in France, Italy, Japan, and other countries.

**(B)**
> Although most people today think of these stories as fairy tales for children, the Grimm brothers first wrote them primarily for adults. Many of their early tales were dark and scary. Later, the brothers changed the text of some of the original stories. They "softened" many of the tales and added drawings. This made them more suitable for children.

**(C)**
> Between 1812 and 1814, the brothers published two books in German. These included stories like "Cinderella," "Snow White," and "Little Red Riding Hood." The collections became known in English as *Grimms' Fairy Tales*.

**(D)**
> The Grimm brothers' tales give a picture of traditional life and beliefs. For example, in the past, many people in Germany believed that forests were dangerous places. In the Grimms' stories, a forest is often the home of evil witches (as in "Hansel and Gretel"), talking animals, and other magical beings.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 동사의 형태나 뜻이 **틀린** 것은?
questions.explanation: pay의 과거분사는 paid이다(pay–paid–paid).

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 문장을 지시대로 바꿀 때 **잘못된** 것은?

> Archeologists found many female skeletons.
choices: Archeologists didn't find many female skeletons. (부정문)
Did archeologists find many female skeletons? (의문문)
Many female skeletons were found by archeologists. (수동태)
Archeologists have find many female skeletons. (현재완료)
Archeologists are finding many female skeletons. (현재진행형)
questions.explanation: 현재완료는 have + 과거분사이므로 have found가 맞다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: Avoid to buy fruit in plastic packaging.
Once there, the boys began to fight.
They want taxing plastic take-out containers.
We should keep to recycle plastic bottles.
questions.explanation: begin은 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 목적어로 쓸 수 있다. ①quit using ②avoid buying ④want to tax ⑤keep recycling.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 중 단어와 뜻이 바르게 짝지어진 것은 모두 몇 개인가?

> extract – 빼내다　　rescue – 구조
> constant – 가끔의　　confusing – 혼란스러운
> refund – 세금　　pollute – 정화하다
> globally – 지역적으로　　container – 용기
questions.explanation: 바른 것: extract, rescue, confusing, container (4개). constant 끊임없는, refund 환불(금), pollute 오염시키다, globally 전 세계적으로.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 품사가 나머지와 **다른** 것은?

> - ⓐ <u>Suddenly</u> the ravens were human again.
> - The raven recognized it ⓑ <u>immediately</u>.
> - She ⓒ <u>accidentally</u> dropped a ring.
> - Many of their ⓓ <u>early</u> tales were dark and scary.
> - The Grimm brothers first wrote them ⓔ <u>primarily</u> for adults.
questions.explanation: ⓓ early는 명사 tales를 꾸미는 형용사(초기의)이다. 나머지는 모두 -ly 부사이다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 어법상 올바른 문장은?
choices: There was seven plates on a table.
On a table, there were seven plates and seven cups.
There is many female skeletons in the cemetery.
Close by, there are a cemetery.
There are something inside its nose.
questions.explanation: There + be동사는 뒤의 주어에 수를 맞춘다. ②복수 → were ①was→were ③is→are ④are→is ⑤are→is.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳은 문장끼리 바르게 짝지은 것은?

> ⓐ The video has viewed millions of times on YouTube.
> ⓑ The soldiers were protect by being underground.
> ⓒ The pyramids were built by ordinary Egyptians.
> ⓓ The turtle was released back into the ocean.
> ⓔ The colors were losing when the soldiers were unearthed.
questions.explanation: 옳은 문장은 ⓒ, ⓓ이다. ⓒⓓ은 바른 수동태. ⓐhas been viewed ⓑwere protected ⓔwere lost.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 것과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?

> <u>Close by</u>, there is a cemetery where the pyramid builders were buried.
questions.explanation: close by는 '바로 가까이에'이므로 Nearby와 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 대화의 빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

> A: I always ______ plastic packaging.
> B: Good for you! How do you do that?
> A: I don't buy fruit or vegetables in plastic packaging.
questions.explanation: 플라스틱 포장 과일·채소를 사지 않는다고 했으므로 '피하다(avoid = stay away from)'가 알맞다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 대화의 내용으로 보아 요약한 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?

> A: When did Denmark place a tax on plastic bags?
> B: It did that in 1993. It was the first country to do it.
>
> → Denmark placed a tax on plastic bags ______ 1993.
questions.explanation: 연도 앞에는 전치사 in을 쓴다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 부분의 쓰임이 밑줄과 같은 것은?

> Eventually, they had a girl <u>who</u> they loved very much.
choices: They were two young men <u>who</u> loved reading stories.
Sea creatures <u>who</u> eat plastic can get hurt.
There lived a man and a woman <u>who</u> had seven sons.
The scientist <u>who</u> we met yesterday studies turtles.
questions.explanation: 주어진 who는 they loved의 목적어 역할을 하는 목적격 관계대명사이다. ⑤도 we met의 목적어. ①②④주격 관계대명사 ③의문사 '누가'.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 <u>rule</u>과 같은 의미로 쓰인 것은?

> Qin Shihuang is remembered for the many things he did during his <u>rule</u>.
choices: As a <u>rule</u>, I get up early.
The king's <u>rule</u> lasted for thirty years.
It's against the <u>rules</u> to run in the hall.
The <u>rule</u> of this game is simple.
questions.explanation: 주어진 rule은 '통치(기간)(a period of control)'. ③왕의 통치가 30년 동안 계속되었다. ①④⑤규칙 ②as a rule 대개.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 영작이 **잘못된** 것은?
choices:
그들은 민담에 관심을 갖게 되었다.
→ They became interested in folktales.

그 모음집은 영어로 'Grimms' Fairy Tales'로 알려지게 되었다.
→ The collections became known in English as *Grimms' Fairy Tales*.

그들은 숲이 위험한 곳이라고 믿었다.
→ They believed that forests were dangerous places.

형제는 독일 전역의 이야기꾼들에게서 민담을 수집하기 시작했다.
→ The brothers began collect folktales from storytellers all over Germany.

이것은 그 이야기들을 어린이에게 더 적합하게 만들었다.
→ This made them more suitable for children.
questions.explanation: begin 뒤에는 to부정사나 동명사가 와야 한다 → began to collect (또는 began collecting).

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 두 문장의 의미가 같도록 바꾼 것이 **잘못된** 것은?
choices:
I wish our sister were here.
→ I'm sorry our sister isn't here.

I wish I knew the answer.
→ I'm sorry I don't know the answer.

I wish I had a special key.
→ I'm sorry I don't have a special key.

I wish the colors lasted longer.
→ I'm sorry the colors don't last longer.

I wish I could fly.
→ I'm sorry I can fly.
questions.explanation: I wish + 과거형은 현재 사실의 반대를 소망한다. I wish I could fly = I'm sorry I can't fly.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 **않는** 것은?
choices: 까마귀들은 사람으로 돌아온 뒤 여동생만 집으로 돌려보냈다.
아버지는 아이에게 줄 물이 필요해 아들들을 숲속 우물로 보냈다.
부부는 딸을 원했고 마침내 딸을 얻었다.
아버지는 아들들이 놀이를 하느라 물을 잊었을 거라고 생각했다.
일곱 번째 까마귀는 여동생이 여기 있으면 자유로워질 수 있다고 말했다.
questions.explanation: they all went home together happily — 오빠들과 여동생 모두 함께 행복하게 집으로 돌아갔다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: According to the passage, why did the father get angry?
choices: Because the boys did not come back with the water for hours.
Because the boys broke the well in the forest.
Because his daughter did not drink the water.
Because the boys turned into ravens.
Because the boys lost his ring.
questions.explanation: 몇 시간이 지나도 아들들이 물을 가지고 돌아오지 않자 놀다가 물을 잊었다고 생각해 화가 났다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Bringing the Terracotta Army's Colors Back
How the Great Wall of China Was Built
The Lives of Farmers in Xi'an
The Writing System of Ancient China
How to Boil an Egg Quickly
questions.explanation: 원래 화려했던 병마용의 색이 사라진 이유와 이를 보존·복원하려는 노력을 다룬다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: The soldiers were always light brown.
The emperor wanted the soldiers to protect his tomb.
Archeologists wash away the dirt around the soldiers.
Artists have already painted the whole army again.
American and French researchers developed the special liquid.
questions.explanation: These, he hoped, would protect his tomb after his death. ①원래는 여러 색 ⑤중국·독일 연구진 ③흙을 건드리지 않는 것이 중요 ④다시 칠하는 방법을 찾는 것이 다음 과제.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 (A) <u>reveal</u>과 의미가 가장 비슷한 것은?
questions.explanation: reveal은 '드러내다(to make something known or visible)'이므로 show와 가장 가깝다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: Which of the following best fits in (B)?
questions.explanation: 대부분의 색이 오늘날까지 '지속되지(last)' 못했다는 뜻이 되어야 한다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 〈보기〉의 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

> Plastic is useful to people because it is strong and lasts a long time. ( ⓐ ) But this is bad news for sea creatures who eat or get stuck in it. ( ⓑ ) According to Savoca, "Single-use plastics are the worst." ( ⓒ ) Some common examples include straws, water bottles, and plastic bags. ( ⓓ ) About 700 sea species (including the turtle from the video) have been caught in or have eaten this kind of plastic. ( ⓔ ) Luckily, the turtle survived and was released back into the ocean.

〈보기〉
> These are items that are used only once before we throw them away.
questions.explanation: 〈보기〉는 Single-use plastics(일회용 플라스틱)의 뜻을 풀이하므로 그 바로 뒤, 예시(straws, water bottles…)가 나오기 전인 ⓒ에 들어가야 한다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: According to the passage, which is **NOT** true?
choices: Scientists are trying to make plastic more biodegradable.
People use a trillion plastic bags worldwide every year.
Denmark was the first country to completely ban plastic bags.
Roughly 10 percent of plastic bags are used in the United States.
Norway recycles 97 percent of its plastic bottles.
questions.explanation: 덴마크는 1993년 비닐봉지에 처음으로 '세금을 매긴(place a tax on)' 나라이다. 완전히 금지했다는 내용은 없다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A)플라스틱 쓰레기를 '줄이는(reduce)' 방법 (B)'재사용' 쇼핑백 (C)병을 넣으면 돌려주는 '환불금(refund)'.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용으로 보아, 미국에서 1년 동안 사용되는 비닐봉지의 수로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 전 세계에서 1년에 1조(a trillion) 개를 쓰고 그중 약 10%가 미국에서 쓰이므로 1조 × 0.1 = 약 1,000억 개이다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 민담 수집(A) → 1812~1814년 두 권 출판(C) → 이야기가 보여 주는 옛 독일의 삶과 믿음(D) → 오늘날은 동화로 여기지만 처음엔 어른용, 나중에 어린이용으로 수정(B).

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글에서 그림 형제의 이야기에 대해 언급되지 **않은** 것은?
choices: 이야기 속 숲은 사악한 마녀나 마법 존재의 집으로 자주 나온다.
초기 이야기 중 많은 것은 어둡고 무서웠다.
나중에 이야기를 부드럽게 고치고 그림을 넣었다.
형제가 직접 영어로 번역해 미국에서 출판했다.
questions.explanation: 형제는 독일어로 책을 냈고, 영어로는 Grimms' Fairy Tales로 '알려졌다'고만 나온다. 직접 번역해 미국에서 출판했다는 내용은 없다.

groups.title: [15~16] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
groups.context:
> Since 2000, there has been a huge increase in worldwide plastic production, but we recycle less than one-fifth of it. A lot of this plastic waste ends up in the ocean. Today, scientists think about 8.1 billion kilograms goes into the sea every year from coastal regions. Most of this plastic will never biodegrade.
>
> This ocean plastic hurts millions of sea animals every year. Some fish eat plastic because it is covered with sea plants, and it looks and smells like food. Typically, eating plastic leads to constant hunger. "Imagine you ate lunch and then just felt weak ... and hungry all day," says marine biologist Matthew Savoca. "That would be very confusing." In some cases, eating sharp pieces of plastic can seriously hurt sea animals and even result in death.
>
> How will plastic affect sea animals in the long term? "I think we'll know the answers in 5 to 10 years' time," says Debra Lee Magadini from Columbia University. But by then, another 25 million tons of plastic will already be in the ocean.

groups.title: [17~20] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
groups.context:
> The world has a plastic problem—and it is increasing. Scientists are working to find a long-term solution by making plastic more biodegradable. But in the meantime, here are five things you can do to reduce plastic waste now.
>
> Quit using plastic bags. Instead, take your own reusable shopping bag to the store. In 1993, Denmark was the first country to place a tax on plastic bags. Today, other countries (such as Chile, Kenya, Indonesia, Germany, and New Zealand) either make customers pay for plastic bags, or have banned them completely.
>
> Skip the straw. Today, around 8.3 billion plastic straws (A) <u>pollute</u> the world's beaches. So when you order a drink, say no to the straw, or bring your own reusable one. In 2018, Seattle became the first major U.S. city to (B)________ plastic straws, and many other cities are set to follow its example.
>
> Don't use plastic bottles. Buy a reusable bottle and fill it with any type of beverage you like. Some cities (like Bundanoon in Australia and San Francisco in the U.S.) have completely or partially banned bottled water. Globally, however, people still buy nearly a million plastic bottles every minute.
>
> Avoid plastic packaging. Buy bar soap instead of liquid soap in plastic containers. Don't buy fruit or vegetables in plastic packaging. In the United Kingdom, leaders are calling for supermarkets to have plastic-free areas. They also want to tax plastic take-out containers.

groups.title: [22~24] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
groups.context:
> Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm were two young men from Germany who loved reading stories. As university students, they became ⓐ <u>interested</u> in folktales—traditional stories or legends that people told again and again, often for generations. The brothers began to (A)________ folktales from storytellers all over Germany. Many were ⓑ <u>similar</u> to stories told in France, Italy, Japan, and other countries. Between 1812 and 1814, the brothers (B)________ two books in German.
>
> The Grimm brothers' tales give a picture of traditional life and beliefs. For example, in the past, many people in Germany believed that forests were ⓒ <u>dangerous</u> places. In the Grimms' stories, a forest is often the home of evil witches (as in "Hansel and Gretel"), talking animals, and other magical beings.
>
> Although most people today think of these stories as fairy tales for children, the Grimm brothers first wrote them primarily for adults. Many of their early tales were dark and ⓓ <u>cheerful</u>. Later, the brothers changed the text of some of the original stories. They ⓔ <u>"softened"</u> many of the tales and added drawings. This made them more (C)________ for children. Like the early tales, though, each story still has a moral: Work hard, be good, and listen to your parents.

groups.title: [25~26] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
groups.context:
**(A)**
> Many people today think of the pyramids of Giza as the defining icon of ancient Egyptian culture. But who actually built them?

**(B)**
> It took about 80 years to build the pyramids. Archeologists believe that about 20,000–30,000 people were involved in the construction. The workers had different roles. Some dug up the rock, some moved it, and some shaped it into blocks. People also worked on different teams, each with its own name.

**(C)**
> Now, however, archeologists have discovered an ancient city near the pyramids. Close by, there is a cemetery where the pyramid builders were buried. From studying these places, archeologists can now confirm that the pyramids were not built by slaves or foreigners (or space aliens!). Ordinary Egyptians built them.

**(D)**
> Life for these workers was hard. "We can see that in their skeletons," says Azza Mohamed Sarry El-Din, a scientist studying bones found in the cemetery. According to her research, the bones show signs of arthritis. However, workers usually had enough food, and they also received medical care if they got sick or hurt.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 동사의 형태나 뜻이 **틀린** 것은?
questions.explanation: sell은 '팔다'이다('사다'는 buy). 형태 sell–sold–sold는 맞지만 뜻이 틀렸다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 문장을 지시대로 바꿀 때 **잘못된** 것은?

> The ravens returned for their meal.
choices: The ravens didn't return for their meal. (부정문)
The ravens will return for their meal. (미래시제)
Do the ravens returned for their meal? (의문문)
The ravens are returning for their meal. (현재진행형)
The ravens were returning for their meal. (과거진행형)
questions.explanation: 과거시제 의문문은 Did + 주어 + 동사원형이므로 Did the ravens return for their meal?이 맞다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: The workers were proud for their work.
The damage to their bones is similar with that of the men.
The world's seas are full of plastic.
The plastic is covered of sea plants.
questions.explanation: be full of(~로 가득 차다)가 옳다. ①proud of ②interested in ③similar to ⑤covered with.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 중 단어와 영영 풀이가 바르게 짝지어진 것은 모두 몇 개인가?

> - collect: to bring together things from different places
> - publish: to print as a book for sale
> - scary: causing fear
> - moment: a very long period of time
> - recognize: to know a person or thing because you have seen them before
> - network: a system of connected roads or parts
> - liquid: a hard solid material
> - compete: to work together without trying to win
questions.explanation: 바른 것: collect, publish, scary, recognize, network (5개). moment는 a very short period of time, liquid는 물처럼 흐르는 물질, compete는 남보다 앞서려고 겨루다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 쓰임이 나머지와 **다른** 것은?

> - Their sister quickly ran ⓐ <u>to</u> them.
> - They were afraid ⓑ <u>to</u> go home.
> - Many were similar ⓒ <u>to</u> stories told in France.
> - Work hard, be good, and listen ⓓ <u>to</u> your parents.
> - Male workers generally lived ⓔ <u>to</u> age 40–45.
questions.explanation: ⓑ는 동사원형 go 앞의 to부정사이다. 나머지는 모두 명사(구) 앞에 쓰인 전치사 to이다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 어법상 올바른 문장은?
choices: Machines make people to return their bottles.
Some countries make customers paying for plastic bags.
The video made people knowing about the problem.
The father made the boys went to the well.
The special liquid helps preserve the soldiers' colors.
questions.explanation: help + (to)동사원형이 옳다. 사역동사 make는 make + 목적어 + 동사원형 → ①return ②pay ④go ③know.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳은 문장끼리 바르게 짝지은 것은?

> ⓐ The soldiers are more lighter in color now.
> ⓑ Khufu's Great Pyramid was the tallest structure in the world for over 3,000 years.
> ⓒ Packaging is used for a more shorter time than other plastic.
> ⓓ Women's lives may have been even tougher than men's.
> ⓔ Plastic lasts longest than paper.
questions.explanation: 옳은 문장은 ⓑ, ⓓ이다. ⓑ최상급 the tallest ⓓ비교급 tougher than(even은 비교급 강조). ⓒmore shorter→shorter ⓐmore lighter→lighter ⓔlongest→longer.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 것과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?

> <u>Globally</u>, however, people still buy nearly a million plastic bottles every minute.
questions.explanation: globally는 '전 세계적으로(in a way that covers the whole world)'이므로 Around the world와 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 대화의 빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

> A: Why are you taking those empty bottles to the supermarket?
> B: The machine there takes bottles. It gives me a ______ for each one, so I get some money back.
questions.explanation: 병을 넣으면 돈을 돌려받으므로 '환불(금)(refund)'이 알맞다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 대화의 내용으로 보아 요약한 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것은?

> A: Where did the father send the seven brothers?
> B: He sent them to a well. It was in the forest.
>
> → The father sent the brothers to a well ______ the forest.
questions.explanation: '숲속에 있는 우물'이므로 a well in the forest가 알맞다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 부분의 쓰임이 밑줄과 같은 것은?

> <u>Since</u> 2000, there has been a huge increase in worldwide plastic production.
choices: <u>Since</u> it was raining, we stayed home.
<u>Since</u> he was sick, he couldn't come.
<u>Since</u> you are tired, you should rest.
<u>Since</u> the bus is late, let's take a taxi.
questions.explanation: 주어진 since는 '~ 이후로'(전치사). ④도 2015년 이후로. ①③②⑤는 '~ 때문에'(이유 접속사).

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 <u>common</u>과 같은 의미로 쓰인 것은?

> Some <u>common</u> examples include straws, water bottles, and plastic bags.
choices: Plastic bags are a <u>common</u> sight on beaches.
Mina and I have a <u>common</u> friend.
The two stories have something in <u>common</u>.
Korea and Japan share a <u>common</u> history.
The park is <u>common</u> land for everyone in the town.
questions.explanation: 주어진 common은 '흔한(happening often; seen in many places)'. ①해변에서 흔히 보이는 것. ②④⑤공통의·공유의 ③in common 공통으로.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 영작이 **잘못된** 것은?
choices:
이 플라스틱 쓰레기 중 많은 양이 결국 바다로 간다.
→ A lot of this plastic waste ends up in the ocean.

플라스틱을 먹는 것은 끊임없는 배고픔으로 이어진다.
→ Eating plastic leads to constant hunger.

그 영상은 유튜브에서 수백만 번 조회되었다.
→ The video has been viewed millions of times on YouTube.

다행히 그 거북이는 살아남았다.
→ Luckily, the turtle survived.

플라스틱은 튼튼하기 때문에 사람들에게 유용하다.
→ Plastic is useful to people because of it is strong.
questions.explanation: because of 뒤에는 명사(구)가 오고, 주어+동사가 오면 because를 쓴다 → because it is strong.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 다음 중 두 문장의 의미가 같도록 바꾼 것이 **잘못된** 것은?
choices:
The colors disappeared because of the air.
→ The colors disappeared because the air.

The boys were afraid, so they didn't go home.
→ Because the boys were afraid, they didn't go home.

Some fish eat plastic because it looks like food.
→ Plastic looks like food, so some fish eat it.

The workers carried heavy things, so they got arthritis.
→ Because the workers carried heavy things, they got arthritis.

It was too late, so he could not take back his words.
→ He could not take back his words because it was too late.
questions.explanation: because는 접속사이므로 뒤에 주어+동사가 와야 한다. 명사 the air만 올 때는 because of를 그대로 써야 한다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 **않는** 것은?
choices: 어떤 물고기는 플라스틱이 바다 식물로 덮여 있어서 먹는다.
5~10년 뒤에는 바다의 플라스틱이 2,500만 톤 줄어들 것이다.
날카로운 플라스틱 조각을 먹으면 해양 동물이 죽을 수도 있다.
Debra Lee Magadini는 5~10년 뒤에 답을 알게 될 것이라고 말했다.
questions.explanation: by then, another 25 million tons of plastic will already be in the ocean — 그때쯤이면 2,500만 톤이 '더' 바다에 들어가 있을 것이다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: What is the main point of the last paragraph?
choices: We already know all the effects of plastic on sea animals.
Sea animals are not affected by plastic in the long term.
Plastic in the ocean will disappear in 10 years.
Scientists at Columbia University stopped studying plastic.
More plastic will enter the ocean before we learn its long-term effects.
questions.explanation: 장기적 영향은 5~10년 뒤에야 알 수 있는데, 그때까지 2,500만 톤의 플라스틱이 더 바다에 들어간다는 경고이다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Why Plastic Is Useful to People
The History of Plastic Bags in Denmark
Easy Ways to Use Less Plastic
The Best Supermarkets in the U.K.
questions.explanation: 지금 당장 플라스틱 쓰레기를 줄이기 위해 할 수 있는 실천법(팁)을 소개하는 글이다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: U.K. leaders want supermarkets to have plastic-free areas.
Bundanoon is a city in the United States.
People buy nearly a million plastic bottles every day.
The writer tells us to buy liquid soap in plastic containers.
Scientists have already made all plastic biodegradable.
questions.explanation: In the United Kingdom, leaders are calling for supermarkets to have plastic-free areas. ③매분(every minute) ②호주 ④고체 비누를 사라 ⑤아직 해결책을 찾는 중.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 (A) <u>pollute</u>와 의미가 가장 비슷한 것은?
questions.explanation: pollute는 '오염시키다(to make water, air, or land dirty and dangerous)'.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: Which of the following best fits in (B)?
questions.explanation: 빨대를 쓰지 말자는 팁이므로 시애틀은 플라스틱 빨대를 '금지한(ban)' 최초의 주요 도시이다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem:
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 〈보기〉의 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

> Today, the soldiers in Xi'an's terracotta museum are light brown, but they weren't always this color. ( ⓐ ) They began as an army of red, blue, yellow, green, white, and purple. ( ⓑ ) Sadly, most of the colors did not last to the present day. ( ⓒ ) Before their discovery, the clay soldiers were protected by being underground. ( ⓓ ) When they were unearthed, however, the air caused the coating under the paint to fall off. ( ⓔ )

〈보기〉
> The paint disappeared in less time than it takes to boil an egg, taking with it important pieces of history.
questions.explanation: 발굴 후 공기 때문에 코팅이 떨어져 나갔다는 원인 뒤에, 그 결과 페인트가 아주 빨리 사라졌다는 〈보기〉가 이어져야 한다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: According to the passage, which is **NOT** true about the Grimm brothers' stories?
choices: Many of them were similar to tales from other countries.
They give a picture of traditional life and beliefs.
Forests in them are usually safe and peaceful places.
The early tales were written mainly for adults.
questions.explanation: 이야기 속 숲은 사악한 마녀·말하는 동물·마법 존재의 집으로, 위험한 곳으로 그려진다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A)이야기꾼들에게서 민담을 '수집하다(collect)' (B)두 권의 책을 '출판했다(published)' (C)어린이에게 더 '적합하게(suitable)'.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 **않은** 것은?
questions.explanation: 초기 이야기는 어둡고 '무서웠다(scary)'. 그래서 나중에 부드럽게 고쳤으므로 cheerful(쾌활한)은 흐름에 맞지 않는다.

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 누가 지었을까?(A) → 고대 도시·묘지 발견으로 일반 이집트인이 지었음을 확인(C) → 80년, 2~3만 명, 역할과 팀(B) → 이 노동자들의 고된 삶과 음식·의료(D).

questions.subject: 영어
questions.stem: 윗글을 읽고 답할 수 있는 질문은?
choices: How tall is Khufu's Great Pyramid?
How much money were the workers paid?
What were the names of the workers' teams?
How long did it take to build the pyramids?
What kind of food did the workers eat?
questions.explanation: It took about 80 years to build the pyramids. 임금, 팀 이름, 피라미드 높이, 음식 종류는 나오지 않는다.
